title: Lithium and the Electric Car

endcard.line: Pictures: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (public domain); Sevenethics (CC0)

segments.say: These bright pools in a Chilean desert are drying out salty water to collect lithium, the lightest metal there is.
Batteries built on lithium store more energy for their weight than other rechargeable kinds, and last for many charges. That is why phones and electric cars use them.

anim.title: Inside a cell
items: Charging: lithium ions move into one electrode
Driving: they flow back to the other

segments.say: Inside, lithium ions slip in and out of two electrode materials. Charging pushes them one way; driving lets them flow back, and that flow powers the car.
Cells like these, packed by the hundreds or thousands, make up an electric car's battery.
Most lithium comes from salty underground brines, like Chile's, or from hard-rock mines, like Australia's.

anim.title: India's search
items: 2023: 5.9 million tonnes (inferred) found in Reasi, J&K
2024: lithium blocks taken up in Argentina

segments.say: In twenty twenty-three, the Geological Survey of India reported five point nine million tonnes of inferred lithium resources in Reasi, Jammu and Kashmir. India has also taken up lithium blocks in Argentina.
For GS Three, treat lithium as a critical mineral: link it to electric mobility, imports and energy security.

sources: Wikipedia, 'Lithium' (read): least dense metal; commonly obtained from brines; Chile estimated (2020) to have the largest reserves, Australia the highest annual production

Wikipedia, 'Lithium-ion battery' (read): rechargeable battery using reversible intercalation of lithium ions into electrode materials; higher specific energy and energy density and longer cycle life than other rechargeable types
PIB, 9 February 2023 (PRID 1897799): GSI established lithium inferred resources (G3) of 5.9 million tonnes in Salal-Haimana, Reasi district, J&K
PIB (PRID 2114466): KABIL signed an exploration and development agreement on 15 January 2024 for five brine-type lithium blocks in Catamarca, Argentina

quiz.q: Where did GSI report inferred lithium resources of 5.9 million tonnes in 2023?
quiz.why: PIB: Salal-Haimana area of Reasi district, J&K.

quiz.q: Why are lithium-ion batteries used in electric cars?
options: They are the cheapest metal batteries
They store more energy for their weight
quiz.why: Higher specific energy and energy density, and a long cycle life.

quiz.q: In Chile's salt flats, lithium is mainly collected by…
quiz.why: Brine is pumped into ponds and left to evaporate.

reviewNote: India facts are from two PIB releases; the battery and lithium basics are from Wikipedia and should be checked against an official source (for example USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries) before approval. 'Inferred' is a low-confidence resource class; the script keeps that word. 'Hundreds or thousands' of cells per car is general knowledge, not sourced. Moving facts: reserve and production rankings change yearly; India's lithium auctions are ongoing.
